question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Naval Presence and Locations in Asia]
options: VOC headquarters in Asia — Batavia (present-day Jakarta, Java)
Dutch conquest of Malacca — 1641, wrested from Portuguese
Dutch fort in India — Pulicat (near Madras) — primary base on Coromandel Coast
Dutch stronghold in Sri Lanka — Colombo, on the western coast
wrong_fact: While the Dutch did control Colombo, their most significant stronghold and capital in Ceylon (Sri Lanka) was Galle on the southwestern coast, not Colombo — though Colombo was also important.
explanation: The VOC (Dutch East India Company) established its Asian headquarters at Batavia (now Jakarta) in 1619 under Jan Pieterszoon Coen. The Dutch captured Malacca from the Portuguese in 1641 with Johor's help. Pulicat (Pulicat Fort/Geldria) was the main Dutch base on the Coromandel Coast. In Sri Lanka, while the Dutch controlled Colombo (captured 1656), Galle on the southwestern coast was their premier fortified stronghold — Galle Fort remains one of the best-preserved Dutch colonial fortifications in Asia.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Naval Battles and their Locations]
options: Battle of the Downs — English Channel (off Kent coast), 1639 — Dutch defeated Spanish Armada
Battle of Colachel — Kerala coast, 1741 — Travancore defeated Dutch fleet
Four Days' Battle — North Sea, 1666 — major Dutch victory over English
Battle of Beachy Head — Atlantic Ocean, 1690 — Dutch-English victory over French
wrong_fact: The Battle of Beachy Head (1690) was fought in the English Channel off the Sussex coast, NOT in the Atlantic Ocean. It was a French victory over the Anglo-Dutch fleet.
explanation: The Battle of the Downs (1639) saw the Dutch Admiral Tromp destroy the Spanish fleet in English waters. The Battle of Colachel (1741) off Kerala was a stunning victory by Travancore's Marthanda Varma over the Dutch — the only Asian victory over a European navy in the 18th century. The Four Days' Battle (1666) in the North Sea was the longest naval battle in history and a major Dutch victory. However, Beachy Head (1690) was fought in the English Channel and was actually a French victory over the combined Anglo-Dutch fleet under Tourville.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dutch Trade Routes and Monopoly Products by Region]
options: Spice monopoly (nutmeg, mace, cloves) — Banda Islands and Moluccas (Maluku), eastern Indonesia
Dutch pepper trade base — Bantam (Banten), western Java
Dutch primary silk and porcelain trade base in China — Guangzhou (Canton) direct trade post
wrong_fact: The Dutch did NOT have a direct trade post at Guangzhou. Their China trade was conducted through Taiwan (Fort Zeelandia, 1624–1662) and later via the licensed trading post at Deshima in Japan — they were barred from direct Canton trade unlike the Portuguese (at Macau).
explanation: The Banda Islands and Maluku (Moluccas) were the world's only source of nutmeg and cloves, which the VOC monopolized violently. Bantam (Banten) in western Java was an early Dutch pepper trade base. Ceylon under Dutch control produced cinnamon which the Dutch monopolized from the mid-17th century. However, the Dutch never had a direct trading post in Guangzhou — they controlled trade with China through Taiwan (Fort Zeelandia until Koxinga expelled them in 1662) and the Dutch trading post in Japan was at Deshima (Dejima) in Nagasaki harbor.
